about.heroBody: Voice Protest is not affiliated with any ideology, political party or institution. It is neutral infrastructure for verified participation, accessible from anywhere and without physical risk.
about.manifesto: "A street protest measures who can be there that day. We measure verifiable support from those who choose to participate — using technical safeguards designed to verify that each adhesion comes from a unique participant connected to the relevant community."
about.sec1Title: What Voice Protest is — and isn't
about.card1Body: Corruption, nepotism, serious negligence, repression, opacity. Against institutions using public money or mandate.
about.card2Body: We don't accept improvement requests, proposals or political preferences. Change.org exists for that.
about.card3Body: Institutions that exercise public functions or use public funds: governments, parliaments, local councils, public universities, public hospitals, public media, among others.
about.card4Body: Every event must include a source — press article, official document or statistical data.
about.card5Body: Demand, denounce, resign, investigate, dismiss. Not: ask, request, propose, thank.
about.card6Body: The form validates verifiable source, type of abuse and action verbs, according to the platform's published rules.
about.geo1Body: Participants who satisfy the national verification criteria. Eligibility is determined through SIM registration and additional geographic signals.
about.geo2Body: Region, province, city, district or institution. Institutional protests may require verification via the corresponding email domain.
about.geo3Body: No geographic restriction. The report shows distribution by country.
about.geo4Body: Each verified phone number can only adhere once to each protest, regardless of the device used.
about.geo5Body: Joining a protest does not prevent joining others of a different scope. National, local and global protests are independent from each other.
about.censo1Body: Verify your membership in a university, hospital, organisation or community with an institutional domain configured for that protest.
about.censo2Body: Accredited members can vouch for new participants. The number of vouches required is configurable per group. Founding groups can be accredited automatically.
about.censo3Body: The email is used solely for verification and transformed into an irreversible HMAC-SHA256 identifier. The original email is not stored persistently.
about.censo4Body: The census is built from real verifications and accredited adhesions. No external member list is imported.
about.seg1Body: Your phone number is used solely for initial verification. It is then transformed into an irreversible HMAC-SHA256 pseudonymous identifier. The original number is not retained after verification is complete.
about.seg2Body: One real number, one adhesion per protest. Significantly reduces duplicate participation and impersonation attempts.
about.seg3Body: Reports include integrity hashes and verifiable public commitments. Anyone can verify that published results match the data recorded at protest closure.
about.openCard1Body: Free API for researchers and journalists. Aggregated data, no authentication required. →
about.openCard2Body: Full source code available under AGPL 3.0 at GitHub.
about.principleNote: Voice Protest verifies participation. It does not verify truth.
about.openCard3Teaser: No advertising. No data sales. No tracking cookies.
about.openCard4Teaser: No institutional funding. No large donors. Individual contributions up to €100.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.principleBody: Voice Protest is built on the principle that democratic participation must not require sacrificing privacy. We collect only what is strictly necessary to verify that each adhesion is real and unique. Voice Protest provides pseudonymous participation — your identity is not visible to other participants and is not retained after verification, but a cryptographic identifier derived from your phone number is kept to prevent duplicate adhesions.
privacy.collect1Title: Cryptographic hash of your phone number
privacy.collect1Body: Your phone number is transmitted over HTTPS to our server solely to send the SMS verification code and to extract your country prefix for geographic eligibility. It is not stored persistently after this process is complete. Only its HMAC-SHA256 hash — a pseudonymous identifier — is retained to prevent duplicate adhesions. The original number cannot reasonably be recovered from the stored identifier.
privacy.collect2Title: Approximate location — city and region only
privacy.collect2Body: If you grant GPS permission, the coordinates are used to determine your city, region and country via the Nominatim service (OpenStreetMap geocoding). This call is always made via our server — never directly from your browser. Nominatim receives our server's IP address, not yours. Coordinates are discarded immediately after geocoding and are never stored in the database.
privacy.collect3Body: Voice Protest generates a random identifier on your device to help prevent duplicate adhesions, abuse of verification systems and automated mass requests. The identifier stored on your device contains no personal information. On our server it is associated with a pseudonymous hash of your phone number — a stable identifier that lets you join later protests without verifying again and prevents duplicate participation. This verified-device record is kept while you keep participating and is deleted after 270 days without any adhesion; if you come back after that, you verify once more by SMS. Because the window resets with each adhesion, the record persists for as long as you remain an active participant.
privacy.collect4Body: Your browser sends an Accept-Language header with each request to our server. Your in-app language preference is stored locally on your device only and is not transmitted separately.
privacy.never1: We do not store your phone number. It is used solely to send the verification SMS and is not retained after that process is complete. Only its HMAC-SHA256 hash — a pseudonymous identifier — is stored.
privacy.never2: We do not use cookies for tracking or advertising.
privacy.never3: Voice Protest does not sell or monetise personal data.
privacy.never4: Voice Protest does not provide direct access to participation data to governments, political parties or institutions. We may be required to comply with lawful court orders under applicable Dutch and EU law.
privacy.never5: We do not display advertising of any kind.
privacy.providersDesc: The following third-party services are used solely to operate the platform. They process data on our behalf and are bound by data processing agreements.
privacy.providerRailway: Backend server infrastructure — US West (California, USA). Data processed by the server (phone number during OTP, GPS coordinates during geocoding) is temporarily transferred to the US. It is not stored in Railway — only in Supabase (EU).
privacy.cookiesBody: Voice Protest does not use tracking cookies or advertising cookies. Language and UI preferences are stored in your browser's localStorage — they never leave your device and require no consent banner.
privacy.retentionBody: Individual, linkable adhesion data — phone-number hash, device identifier, nullifier and fine-grained location — is irreversibly anonymised 90 days after a protest closes: these fields are permanently set to null. Only non-identifying aggregates remain (country, GPS-confirmed flag, reliability score). The auditable snapshot (integrity_records) and the public report are kept indefinitely and contain only aggregated statistics with no personal data. The verified-device record — the link between your device identifier and the pseudonymous hash of your phone number — follows its own rule: it is deleted after 270 days without any adhesion, and re-created (with one SMS verification) if you return.
privacy.sourceNote: All source code is publicly auditable under AGPL 3.0 licence.
privacy.reportNoteBody: The public report generated by each protest contains only aggregated statistics — total adhesions, geographic distribution, reliability breakdown. It contains no personally identifiable data and is designed to remain accessible indefinitely. It is the public, auditable record of verified participation.
privacy.metadataBody: For each adhesion we store: HMAC-SHA256 hash of phone number, city and region (from geocoding), random device identifier, reliability score (60–95%), geographic signals used (GPS / SIM / IP), approximate timestamp (rounded to the nearest hour) and a boolean confirming whether GPS was active. We document these data transparently and in full because we believe participants have the right to know exactly what information is retained.
privacy.pushBody: If you choose to enable push notifications after joining a protest, your browser's push endpoint — a technical identifier assigned by your browser provider (Google, Mozilla, etc.) — is stored linked to that protest. This endpoint is used solely to send you the result notification and is deleted when the protest closes. Enabling notifications slightly reduces your pseudonymity. It is entirely optional and requires your explicit consent.
privacy.abuseBody: To protect verification resources and prevent automated use of the platform, Voice Protest may temporarily record pseudonymous technical identifiers — such as HMAC-SHA256 hashes of phone numbers, pseudonymous IP hashes and random device identifiers. These records are used exclusively to prevent fraud, spam and abuse of verification systems. They are automatically deleted after 7 days.
privacy.gpsStorageNote: GPS coordinates are temporarily stored in the browser's local storage solely to pass them between screens during the adhesion process. They are deleted immediately after the adhesion is registered — before the process completes. They are never sent to any server in their original form, nor retained in the browser after the process ends.
privacy.nullifiersBody: To ensure each phone number can only adhere once per protest, the system calculates a nullifier — a unique identifier derived from the phone hash and protest identifier — and verifies it does not already exist. The nullifier is never published. Instead, at protest closure, public commitments — SHA256(protest_id + nullifier) — are generated, allowing anyone to verify the report integrity hash without revealing identities or enabling cross-protest correlation.
privacy.integrityRecordsBody: At protest closure, the data needed for public verification — public commitments, geographic distribution, integrity hash — are saved in a permanent record (integrity_records). This record survives the 90-day anonymisation of individual adhesions, designed to remain available long-term.
privacy.institutionalEmailBody: For protests with institutional verification, the participant provides an email address from the configured domain. This email is used solely to send the OTP verification code. Like the phone number, the original email is not stored — it is transformed into an irreversible HMAC-SHA256 hash. The email is never used for subsequent communications or shared with the protest convener.
privacy.donationsBody: Donations are processed through external payment providers (such as Ko-fi and PayPal), which may process the donor's personal data — name, email, payment details — as part of completing the transaction. Voice Protest does not store the donor's identity, email or payment information. The platform records only the donation amount, currency, payment provider, timestamp and a non-identifying technical reference, used solely to update the protest's funding balance and the platform sustainability fund.
privacy.providerNominatim: GPS geocoding — converts coordinates into city, region and country. All calls are made via our backend server. Nominatim receives our server's IP address, never the user's.
privacy.providerGithub: Static frontend hosting (voiceprotest.org). GitHub Pages may receive the IP address of each visitor when serving the application files.
privacy.pushTimezone: If you activate push notifications, we may also store your device's timezone to avoid sending non-essential alerts during nighttime hours (23:00–07:00 local time). This information is used exclusively to schedule notifications and is deleted alongside your subscription when the event closes.
privacy.providerIpapi: IP geolocation — estimates country, city and region from the IP address. Raw IP is not stored.
privacy.ipGeoProxy: Voice Protest may use the IP address received by its backend server to estimate country, city and region through an external IP geolocation provider. The raw IP address is not stored. Only the approximate result may be used as a geographic reliability signal.

funding.title: Funding & Independence Policy
funding.principleBody: Voice Protest exists to provide an independent infrastructure for verified civic participation. Independence is a fundamental requirement of the platform. Voice Protest seeks to fund its operating costs through voluntary contributions from individuals, without financial control or influence from governments, political parties, companies or institutions.
funding.costsTitle: What it costs to run Voice Protest
funding.costsDesc: Voice Protest operates at minimal cost. Full transparency on current infrastructure:
funding.smsCost: 💬 SMS verification generates a variable cost per verification attempt — typically a few cents, depending on country, provider and retries. Contributions associated with a protest help cover these technical costs. Participating does not require payment.
funding.accept1: Individual contributions from any person, up to the applicable per-donation limit.
funding.accept2: Small recurring contributions to cover operational costs.
funding.accept3: Contributions directed at covering infrastructure, security audits or technical improvements.
funding.accept4: Contributions from people who believe in the value of verified, independent participation.
funding.reject1: Funding from political parties, governments or state institutions.
funding.reject2: Corporate, institutional or any funding from entities seeking to influence the governance, moderation or decisions of the platform. Voice Protest does not seek this type of funding. When a contribution is identifiable as coming from an entity that would compromise the independence of the project, it may be refused or returned.
funding.reject3: Donations conditioned on any change to platform behaviour, content moderation or results.
funding.reject5: Revenue from the sale or commercialisation of user data.
funding.reject6: Funding that would create any conflict of interest with the platform's independence.
funding.independenceBody: Financial contributions do not grant control over the platform, its governance or any protest published on it. Donors do not receive privileged access, visibility advantages or the ability to influence moderation decisions. The editorial and technical independence of the platform is non-negotiable. If Voice Protest cannot be sustained through independent individual contributions, it will reduce its operational capacity rather than compromise this principle.
funding.supportBody: If you believe in verified, independent participation, you can support the platform's operating costs through Ko-fi. Contributions go towards SMS, email, servers, domain, security and audits. The project is currently developed voluntarily and contributions are not used to pay salaries.
funding.transparencyNote: All source code is publicly auditable under AGPL 3.0.
funding.transparencyBody: Voice Protest maintains an internal financial record covering donations, operating costs and platform fund movements. Public transparency reports will be published progressively as the platform grows. The first report will be published when there is sufficient financial activity for the information to be meaningful. Voice Protest does not sell influence. Contributions only help cover the technical costs needed for verified participants to participate.
funding.donationsNote: Donations made through Ko-fi are registered automatically. Individual contributions are capped at €100 per donation to keep financing participatory. Donations received through other channels may still be registered manually.
funding.donorPrivacyNote: Ko-fi and PayPal may know your name and email as payment processors. Voice Protest does not store your identity — only the donation amount and currency are recorded to update this event's funding balance.
funding.noInfluenceTitle: Voice Protest does not sell influence
funding.verificationProtectionBody: Voice Protest applies technical measures to prevent abusive verification code requests, automated attempts and malicious consumption of resources. These measures help protect the funds allocated to SMS and email verification so they can be used for genuine participation.
funding.splitBody: Donations directed to a specific protest are split between: 90% allocated to that protest's verification budget, and 10% allocated to the platform sustainability fund. This split may be adjusted in the future and will always be publicly documented.
funding.surplusBody: When a protest closes with unused verification funds, the remaining balance may be transferred to the platform sustainability fund and used exclusively for infrastructure, verification systems, security audits and platform maintenance.
funding.allocationBody: Contributions may be divided between protest verification resources and the long-term sustainability of Voice Protest. The allocation model is publicly documented and may evolve as the project matures. Donations made from a specific event's screen are automatically assigned to that event's verification balance. Donations made directly through Ko-fi without a reference to a specific event are credited to the platform sustainability fund.
funding.sustainabilityBody: The sustainability fund exists to preserve the long-term independence of Voice Protest. It may be used for hosting, security, verification systems, audits and future maintenance of the platform.
funding.limitBody: To preserve the independence and participatory nature of the project, individual contributions are currently limited to €100 per donation. The purpose is that protests are funded collectively by many participants, not promoted by a single large donor. If a payment above this limit is received, only €100 is registered as a computable contribution. Any excess is held for manual review and is not automatically credited to the protest balance or the platform fund.
funding.corporateNote: Voice Protest is funded primarily through small individual contributions. It does not seek funding from companies, political parties, public administrations or organisations seeking to influence the governance of the project.

evidence.title: What this report proves — and what it does not
evidence.outsideScopeTitle: Outside the scope of this report

demonstrates.unique_participation_phone: Unique, verified participation: each adhesion comes from a distinct verified phone number, counted once per convocatoria.
demonstrates.unique_participation_email: Unique, verified participation: each adhesion comes from a distinct verified institutional email address, counted once per convocatoria.
demonstrates.sim_country: Each participant holds a SIM registered in {country}.
demonstrates.country_breakdown: The country of each participant is recorded and shown in the geographic breakdown.
demonstrates.local_verified_municipality: {count} of {total} adhesions were geographically verified: GPS placed the participant inside the declared municipality ({territory}), matched against its OpenStreetMap entity.
demonstrates.local_verified_region: {count} of {total} adhesions were geographically verified: GPS placed the participant inside the declared region ({territory}), matched against its OpenStreetMap entity.
demonstrates.institutional_affiliation: Each participant holds a verified email address in the institutional domain {domain}. This provides evidence supporting institutional affiliation.
demonstrates.census_vouching: Affiliation is additionally supported by peer vouching within the institutional census.
demonstrates.public_auditability: The result is auditable: the closed report carries an integrity hash and records per-adhesion public commitments. Full independent public verification, with complete disclosure of those commitments, is available from integrity version 2.

not.affiliation_geographic: That participants belong to any specific affected community: no territorial or institutional membership was verified.
not.region_presence: That participants are physically in {territory}: regional scope is a declaration by the creator, and participants are verified as national, not as present in the region.
not.residence: That participants are legally resident in {territory}: GPS is a verification signal, not proof of residence, and can be spoofed.
not.institutional_role: The participant's role or status within the institution (for example active student versus staff), nor that the whole institution is represented.
not.truth: That the reported facts are true: Voice Protest records verified participation, not the validity of the claim.
not.representative: That the result represents the entire affected population: it measures those who chose to participate.

methods.sms_otp: SMS one-time-password verification of a real phone number (Twilio Verify).
methods.census_vouching: Peer vouching within the institutional census.
methods.gps_osm_municipality: GPS reverse-geocoded against the OpenStreetMap entity of the declared municipality ({territory}).
methods.gps_osm_region: GPS reverse-geocoded against the OpenStreetMap entity of the declared region ({territory}).
methods.ip: Approximate IP geolocation, used as a secondary signal (not stored in plain text).

admission.public_institution: Recipient is a public institution, verified on Wikidata ({wikidata}).
admission.abuse_category: A specific public-abuse category was declared: {category}.
admission.source_accepted: A documentary source was provided and accepted.
admission.petition_filter: The source passed the petition-platform filter (change.org, avaaz.org, etc. are rejected).
admission.wikidata_verified: Recipient validation was performed server-side via the Wikidata API.
